chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Husayn ibn Bishshar from Abd Allah ibn Junadib from Muawiya ibn Wahb said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The month that is said to be the one that does not decrease, Dhul-Qadah, is not the one with the most decrease among the months of the year.' And as for the saying that the year is three hundred and fifty-five days because the heavens and the earth were created in six days which were deducted from three hundred and sixty days, this does not necessitate that a specific month of them is always thirty days. Rather, it implies that the six days are distributed among all the months without specific detail or specification, for what is deficient in them coincides with being complete as a substitute for being deficient. And as for the saying that the months of the year differ in completeness and deficiency, having a complete month and a deficient month, this also does not necessitate the opponent's claim regarding the month of Ramadan what he claimed, nor regarding Sha'ban what he ruled regarding its deficiency, in any case. Because they may be in accordance with what the description included of completeness and deficiency, but they are not in that order and system. Rather, it is not denied that two consecutive months coincide in completeness and two consecutive months in deficiency, and three months as well as we described, and this is in agreement with the saying that there is a deficient month and a complete month, since in the explicit text of the hadith there is no mention of continuity or separation.

And as for what Ibn Rabah narrated from Sama'ah from al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfa from Muawiya ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding His Exalted Saying, 'And to complete the number,' he said, 'Fasting of thirty days.' And this report is also similar to what preceded, that it is a single report which does not necessitate knowledge or action, and the discussion about it is like the discussion about others, that it is not permissible to oppose it with the apparent meaning of the Quran. And that is that ruling the completion of the number for fasting as thirty days does not prevent its completion in the month if it fasts twenty-nine days, because what is meant by completing the number is the days which are the days of the month in any case. And there is no disagreement that the month which is twenty-nine days is a month in reality, not metaphor. And we do not deny that it is obligatory upon us, when there is a doubt in the crescent of Shawwal, to complete the month as thirty days, and that this is also obligatory with knowledge of the completion of the month. And if the matter is as we described, the attachment to the hadith in opposition to the known from the Sharia falls away. And as for the report that was narrated:

key_terms.إِكْمَالُ الْعِدَّةِ: Completing the number, referring to the Quranic verse about fasting thirty days
key_terms.النُّقْصَان: Deficiency, referring to a month having twenty-nine days
key_terms.الْكَمَال: Completeness, referring to a month having thirty days
key_terms.ذُو الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhul-Qadah, the eleventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.هِلَالُ شَوَّالٍ: The crescent of Shawwal, marking the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars calculate the length of lunar months and the number of fasting days in Ramadan?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration to resolve the tension between the fixed lunar calendar and the variable nature of month lengths, emphasizing that the Quranic command to 'complete the number' (2:185) refers to the actual days present rather than a rigid thirty-day requirement. This scholarly analysis supports the Shia practice of completing Ramadan or Sha'ban to thirty days only when the new moon is obscured (ikmal), while acknowledging that a twenty-nine-day month is equally valid in reality. It refutes the argument that specific months must always be full or deficient, allowing for flexible arrangements that do not contradict established Sharia principles.
